articles.title: American exodus: why do so many US NHL stars want out of Canada?
articles.summary: Players across the league are leaving their teams up north to return home. It’s prompted questions around money, tax rates, geopolitics and respect. Back in September 1925, Frederick Wilson, sports editor at the Globe, explained the fear among hockey fans that Canadian teams might not be able to…
body: At the time, Wilson reassured everyone that, no matter the big US cash, everyone on the ice would be Canadian anyway. “It will be some years before the [US] will be in a position to furnish players,” he wrote. He was right about that. It took a long time for the US to catch up to Canada in on-ice talent. But now that it has, should we expect Americans to want to play anywhere else than the US? For 100 years Canada has worried that the US would just buy all the best hockey players. But now it makes its own and, as the new NHL season gets underway on Tuesday night, they want to go home.

It’s difficult to pinpoint where this all started. But the general feeling, given the timing, is that something happened around this year’s Olympics that prompted US-born players to turn their backs on Canada. Maybe it started earlier, in 2025, after the 4 Nations Face-Off. Or maybe it was just in the wind, given the new geopolitical tensions between the two countries. In any event, as the 2026-27 NHL season kicks off Tuesday, the divide is back – or at least seems to have deepened.

It’s prompted questions around money, tax rates, geopolitics and respect.

articles.title: 'Period of deception' - Pochettino on Man City verdict
articles.summary: Former Tottenham and Chelsea manager Mauricio Pochettino says it is "impossible to turn back time" after Manchester City being found guilty of financial breaches.
body: Former Tottenham and Chelsea manager Mauricio Pochettino says "we have lived through a period of deception" after Manchester City were found guilty of breaking the majority of the charges brought against them by the Premier League.
An independent panel found City to be guilty of a wide range of financial rule breaches, with the Athletic, external reporting on Friday that 114 of the 115 charges against them have been upheld.
Sanctions are yet to be announced, but City plan on appealing against the decision.
The charges relate to a period from 2009-10 to 2017-18, while they were accused of a failure to co-operate with Premier League investigations between December 2018 to February 2023.

In another cute piece of trivia, Australia’s head coach Tony Popovic shadowed Carlo Ancelotti at AC Milan as he was starting out on his coaching journey while still a player at Crystal Palace. Now they’re facing each other across the dugout. The master v the apprentice.
The two nations are separated by 23 spots on the FIFA men’s rankings, but based on last week’s game, you really couldn’t tell. Might we see a little bit more history made tonight?

articles.title: Today in Boston Celtics history: Chuck Cooper, Brad Lohaus, Art Williams born
articles.summary: He played college basketball at West Virginia State before transferring to Duquesne, his time at the former interrupted by his draft to serve in World War II. Later the Celtics selected Cooper with the 14th overall pick in the 1950 NBA Draft.
body: In and of itself, a player being taken from a respected university in what was then the second round of the draft ought to have been an unremarkable event save one major detail – Cooper would be the first Black player drafted in NBA history. This momentous occasion was, as one might expect given the era, questioned by the other team owners in the league when they heard that Celtics General Manager Red Auerbach planned to draft Cooper. This prompted Celtics owner Walter A. Brown to famously say "I don't give a damn if he's striped, plaid or polka dot. Boston takes Charles Cooper of Duquesne."
Cooper played four seasons with the Celtics, over which he averaged 6.8 points, 6.6 rebounds, and 1.8 assists per game.

It is also the birthday of former Celtics big man Brad Lohaus, born today in 1956 in New Ulm, Minnesota. Taken by the Celtics out of Iowa with the 45th pick of the 1987 NBA Draft, Lohaus for parts of two seasons. He was dealt with current Boston team president and former shooting guard Danny Ainge to the Sacramento Kings for Joe Kleine and Ed Pinckney, averaging 4.8 points and 2.4 rebounds per game with the team.

articles.title: Keenum rolls back years to lead Chicago Bears to win over Philadelphia Eagles
articles.summary: Case Keenum passed for two touchdowns in his first NFL start in almost three years as Chicago Bears shut down Jalen Hurts and the Philadelphia Eagles for a 27-7 victory on Monday night.
body: Stepping in for Caleb Williams, Keenum starred completing 24 passes from 34 attempts to make 247 yards. He also scored his first rushing touchdown since 2019 on a one-yard plunge with seven minutes and 19 seconds left to play, capping a 13-play drive that took more than eight minutes off the clock.
It was Keenum's first action since he started for Houston in a 36-22 loss to Cleveland in December 2023.
"To get a shot again like this? You dream of it," Keenum said. "That's why I'm still here doing this when I get knocked down.
"I got knocked down my whole career. I just keep getting up, coming to work, just keep bouncing back."

articles.title: Poch: We lived through a period of deception if Man City guilty
articles.summary: Former Tottenham and Chelsea manager Mauricio Pochettino says the Premier League "lived through a period of deception" if Manchester City breached financial rules.
body: Reports on Friday claimed an independent tribunal had reached its decisions in Manchester City’s 115-charge case - and that virtually all were found to have been proven; Man City deny all wrongdoing; Pochettino said: "If it's true…we've lived through a period of deception."

Reports last Friday said an independent tribunal has reached decisions in Manchester City's 115-charge case between the league and the club, and Sky Sports News understands the process is moving to the appeal stage.
Pochettino, who was in charge of Spurs from 2014 to 2019 and Chelsea in 2023-24, having previously managed Southampton from 2013 to 2014, said it had warped the view of history.

Pochettino told the Guardian, through an interpreter: "At the end of the day, we went through something where sporting fairness didn't exist, so how do you repair everything that was damaged because of that?
